name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A vehicle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Defined by NMSA 1978 §66-1-4.5 and regulated by §§66-3-708 and 66-3-709, enacted by SB 69 (2023).

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts
Class 1 and class 3 assist only while the rider is pedaling, stopping at 20 and 28 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling, up to 20 mph
On class 1 and class 3, a mechanism that can't be bypassed cuts the motor when the rider stops pedaling; on class 2 the motor cuts out when the brakes are applied
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its speed capability or motor engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Riders under 16 may not operate a class 3, but may ride as a passenger on one designed to carry passengers
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a protective helmet, under the Child Helmet Safety Act
Class 1 may be ridden on bicycle or pedestrian paths where bicycles may go, unless the local government bans it
Class 2 and class 3 are kept off bicycle and pedestrian paths unless the path is within a street or highway or the local government allows them
On a natural-surface trail designated non-motorized, the state agency or local government managing it decides whether it's allowed
Not a motor vehicle or off-highway motor vehicle: exempt from registration and title
A two- or three-wheeled electric vehicle that isn't an electric-assisted bicycle and can exceed 20 mph on motor power alone is an electric mobility device, which is a motor vehicle
